criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First line names subject + role + the concrete recent decision (no-cost, noncompetitive 20,000-acre transfer listing scalable data centers) and fits inside the ~210 char cutoff; second line adds the legal-challenge stake. Decision is the hook, not bio.

criteria.name: Subject + decision load-bearing for AK
criteria.notes: Public authority ED whose choice materially affects AK energy siting and AI capital; concrete consequence named (Railbelt grid, Anchorage ratepayers, Mat-Su, DNR decision weeks away, January legislature). No hard dollar figure, but the no-cost transfer value is the stake.

criteria.name: Subject identification fidelity
criteria.notes: Full name, role (Executive Director), and org (AIDEA, state development-finance authority) in body with explicit Anchorage tie; every fact matches the dossier.

criteria.name: Decision specificity + primary-source
criteria.notes: What + when + binary stated clearly ('He could have paused for project-level review. He pressed forward.'), attributed to Alaska Beacon primary source, corroboration independent, date within the applied 60-day window. Letter date not pinned to a fetched doc, handled honestly.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Takes an honest, evidence-led position ('sharp aim, mediocre sequencing'), credits the shovel-ready-land logic and names the mechanism risk proportionately. Matches post_001 energy, not boosterism or manufactured criticism.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Names DNR's pending final decision and its window, plus specific triggers to watch (tenant naming, Railbelt interconnection filing, senator escalation to legislation/litigation in January).

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, plainspoken, Alaska-first, business-literate; no press-release cadence, no hagiography, no influencer tics.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Word count 446 and total chars under 3000 with a one-sentence bio, but two paragraphs (140 and 181 words) ran as walls of text. Orchestrator applied the scorer's fix mechanically after scoring: the two dense paragraphs were split at sentence boundaries with no word changes (final_post.md now has 8 paragraphs).

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Closes with a real, debatable question tied to the specific convey-now-vs-wait binary; no CTA, no rhetorical softener.

criteria.name: Credibility guard
criteria.notes: Minimal bio, substantial decision treatment, every claim traceable to corroborated evidence; praise and critique both earned, none recycled or invented.

one_sentence_fix: Split the two dense middle paragraphs (the DNR/senators recap and the analysis paragraph) into 2-to-4-sentence chunks so the post scans cleanly on mobile.
post_scoring_edit: Paragraph breaks only, applied by the orchestrator per one_sentence_fix; no words changed, chars 2906.
